chunks: 3506 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who was under an obligation to free a slave, but died before he could free one. Then his son went and bought a man from his own earnings and freed him on behalf of his father. After that, the freed man acquired wealth, then died and left it behind. For whom would his inheritance be? He said, so he replied:
"If the slave that had been due upon his father was in fulfillment of a vow, or gratitude, or was obligatory upon him, then the freed man is a sa'ibah, and no one has any claim over him."

He said: "Then if he had affiliated himself, before dying, to one of the Muslims, and he guaranteed his offense and liability, he would be his mawla and his heir, if he had no Muslim relative to inherit from him. And if he had not affiliated himself to anyone until he died, then his inheritance belongs to the Imam, the Imam of the Muslims, if he has no relative from the Muslims to inherit from him."

He said: "And if the slave due from his father was voluntary, and his father had instructed him to free a person on his behalf, then the wala' of the freed man is an inheritance for all the children of the deceased."
He said: "And the one who bought him and then freed him by his father's instruction is like one of the heirs, when the freed man does not have free Muslim relatives who inherit from him."

He said: "And if his son, who bought the slave and freed him on behalf of his father from his own wealth after his father's death, did so voluntarily from himself without his father having instructed him to do that, then his wala' and inheritance belong to the one who bought him from his own wealth and freed him on behalf of his father, if the freed man has no heir from among his kin."

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the rightful authority of the Muslims who inherits in the absence of other heirs
key_terms.الْمُعْتَقَ: the person who was freed from slavery
key_terms.جَرِيرَتَهُ: his legal burden or indemnity assumed by an affiliate
key_terms.جِنَايَتَهُ: his offense or liability requiring responsibility
key_terms.سَائِبَةٌ: a freed person over whom no private claim of wala' is held
key_terms.عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ: the manumission of a slave as a legal obligation
key_terms.وَلَاءَ: the bond of patronage and inheritance resulting from manumission

ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a freed slave when a son emancipates him on behalf of his deceased father?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning the inheritance and wala' of a freed slave when a son emancipates someone on behalf of his deceased father. It distinguishes between emancipation done to fulfill an obligatory duty, one done by the father's instruction voluntarily, and one done solely by the son's own voluntary initiative, assigning inheritance differently in each case. It also states that if the freed person has no kin and no allegiance with a Muslim patron, his inheritance returns to the Imam of the Muslims.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3506 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), about a man who was obligated to free a slave but died before doing so. His son then purchased a slave with his own wealth and freed him on behalf of his father. Later, the freed slave acquired wealth and passed away, leaving an inheritance.
I asked: "Who inherits from him?"

Imam (as) replied: "If the obligation to free the slave was due to a vow, gratitude, or was otherwise obligatory upon his father, then the freed slave is a sa'ibah (freed without claim of ownership), and no one has any claim over him."

Imam (as) continued: "However, if the freed slave had allied himself (by appointing a guardian) to one of the Muslims before dying, and that guardian accepted responsibility for his offenses and liabilities, then the guardian becomes his master and inherits from him-if the freed slave has no Muslim relatives to inherit from him."
"If the freed slave did not appoint a guardian before dying, then his inheritance goes to the Imam of the Muslims-provided he has no Muslim relatives to inherit from him."

Imam (as) further said: "If the obligation to free the slave was voluntary, and the father had instructed his son to free a slave on his behalf, then the wala' (bond of loyalty) of the freed slave and his inheritance belong to all the children of the deceased."
"In this case, the son who purchased and freed the slave based on his father's instructions is counted as one of the heirs-unless the freed slave has free Muslim relatives who can inherit from him."

Imam (as) added: "If the son purchased and freed the slave after his father's death voluntarily, without any instruction from his father, then the wala' and inheritance of the freed slave belong to the son who freed him-provided the freed slave has no inheriting relatives from among his kin."
